docs.t: Judge Fernando Rodriguez Jr. (S.D. Tex.) — Extensions and continuances (trap)
docs.x: Judge Fernando Rodriguez Jr., S.D. Tex.. Extensions and continuances (trap): Seek extensions of Scheduling Order deadlines before they expire; late requests are disfavored. Counsel may agree to continue discovery past the deadline, but the court will not intervene, and post-deadline discovery won’t justify a continuance absent exceptional circumstances. Once trial is set, continuances only for extraordinary circumstances. Joint motions are not binding, and witness unavailability won’t continue a trial; be ready with written or videotaped deposition or stipulation.

docs.t: Judge Fernando Rodriguez Jr. (S.D. Tex.) — Appearances
docs.x: Judge Fernando Rodriguez Jr., S.D. Tex.. Appearances: An attorney appearing must know the case, have authority to bind the client, and be counsel of record. Request a telephone or video appearance by email to the Case Manager as far ahead as reasonably possible, telling opposing counsel. Notify the Case Manager immediately when a matter set for trial or hearing is resolved.

docs.t: Judge Fernando Rodriguez Jr. (S.D. Tex.) — Initial pretrial conference (trap)
docs.x: Judge Fernando Rodriguez Jr., S.D. Tex.. Initial pretrial conference (trap): Plaintiff (or the removing party) must serve the Order Setting Initial Pretrial Conference on opposing parties. Serve defendants within 90 days of filing or risk sua sponte dismissal under Rule 4(m). File a list of all financially interested entities and attorneys within 15 days of receiving the order, underlining publicly traded corporations. File the Joint Discovery/Case Management Plan (court’s 20-item form, restating each instruction) at least 3 business days before the conference; discuss any requested changes to the Preliminary Scheduling Order at the Rule 26(f) conference. Counsel must have interviewed clients, read readily available documents, and discussed ADR. The court may rule on pending motions or cancel the conference if nothing needs attention; noncompliance can bring sanctions including dismissal

docs.t: Judge Fernando Rodriguez Jr. (S.D. Tex.) — Civil pretrial
docs.x: Judge Fernando Rodriguez Jr., S.D. Tex.. Civil pretrial: Plaintiff files the Joint Pretrial Order by the Scheduling Order deadline, with four exhibit lists and four witness lists per party and a statement that settlement efforts are exhausted. Each party separately files, in duplicate, proposed voir dire and a proposed charge with authority (jury) or proposed findings, agreed and contested separated, and conclusions with authority (bench). Motions in limine and objections to exhibits and witnesses are due by the Scheduling Order deadline; failure to object in writing concedes authenticity and admissibility. (The older standalone Joint Pretrial Order form instead requires authenticity objections within 5 days after listing and other objections at least 3 business days before trial.) The Final Pretrial Conference is set for 1:30 p.m.; jury selection and trial dates are set there. Be prepar

docs.t: Judge Fernando Rodriguez Jr. (S.D. Tex.) — Civil trial
docs.x: Judge Fernando Rodriguez Jr., S.D. Tex.. Civil trial: Usually 12 jurors and one alternate. Trial normally runs 9 a.m. to 5:30 p.m., with lunch from noon to 1:30 p.m. Plaintiff takes the table nearer the jury. Question witnesses from the podium; counsel instruct their witnesses on “the Rule” if invoked. The court conducts initial voir dire, then allots time to counsel. Mark exhibits before the Final Pretrial Conference and give the court a tabbed, indexed notebook. Unobjected exhibits are admitted first. Provide photos of bulky exhibits, and request return of exhibits within 30 days after trial or they may be destroyed. Bring any equipment beyond easels, laptop connections, and the document camera (e.g., for PowerPoint) and tell the Case Manager in advance. No real-time reporting. Counsel may contact jurors after trial in civil cases.

docs.t: Judge Fernando Rodriguez Jr. (S.D. Tex.) — Settlements and minors
docs.x: Judge Fernando Rodriguez Jr., S.D. Tex.. Settlements and minors: On settlement, file a Rule 41 stipulation of dismissal or a Joint Notice with an estimated time for dismissal papers; the court then vacates settings and sets a deadline. Minor plaintiffs: if there is a potential conflict with the parent or guardian, jointly move for an attorney ad litem before mediation or ADR; if none, jointly move for one for the settlement hearing. If no agreement, each side proposes two names. All parties and attorneys must attend the settlement hearing unless excused.

docs.t: Judge Fernando Rodriguez Jr. (S.D. Tex.) — Criminal cases (trap)
docs.x: Judge Fernando Rodriguez Jr., S.D. Tex.. Criminal cases (trap): File a courtesy hard copy with the District Clerk’s Office, the same day, of any submission totaling 20 pages or more; conventional filing over 50 pages, double-sided, or oversized needs leave. Send a hard copy of emergency motions to the Case Manager. Responses due in 21 days (silence is agreement), replies within 10 days; briefs limited to 20 pages. Motions to dismiss, sever, or for separate trial are due at least 30 days before jury selection. Continuance motions must state the Speedy Trial Act exception and length requested. After a plea before a magistrate judge, the plea is accepted unless the defendant moves to withdraw or objects within 14 days and schedules a hearing within 30 days. PSR objections are due within 14 days of receipt. Sentencings are at 8:30 a.m.; re-arraignments follow the Final Pretrial Conference. M

docs.t: Judge Fernando Rodriguez Jr. (S.D. Tex.) — Courtroom etiquette
docs.x: Judge Fernando Rodriguez Jr., S.D. Tex.. Courtroom etiquette: Stand when addressing or addressed by the court, speak only to the court (except witnesses and the jury), avoid bench conferences without permission, and hand items for the judge to the Case Manager. Ask permission to approach a witness or to conduct a demonstration. Parties and counsel must remain during jury deliberations; absence waives the right to attend the verdict. Comply with the Texas Disciplinary Rules and Texas Lawyer’s Creed.

docs.t: Judge Terrence G. Berg (E.D. Mich.) — Discovery disputes (trap)
docs.x: Judge Terrence G. Berg, E.D. Mich.. Discovery disputes (trap): Do not file any discovery motion without leave; it will be stricken without notice. First confer by phone or in person (email alone is insufficient), then call the case manager for a status conference. The court may resolve the dispute by phone or refer it to a magistrate judge, possibly for briefing. Needing the court after a magistrate judge could not resolve a dispute is treated as a sign of impropriety or uncooperativeness, and delay draws costs. Represented parties will rarely get leave to file discovery motions against a self-represented party.

docs.t: Judge Terrence G. Berg (E.D. Mich.) — Motions and briefs (trap)
docs.x: Judge Terrence G. Berg, E.D. Mich.. Motions and briefs (trap): Strict compliance with L.R. 7.1(a) concurrence; costs are imposed for failure, and the opponent may email the case manager and efile_berg@mied.uscourts.gov right away to report it. Page limits (L.R. 7.1(d)(3)) and 14-point, double-spaced format (L.R. 5.1(a)) are enforced. Oversized-brief requests must be made by motion at least 2 days before the due date, stating reasons and pages sought. A brief plus exhibits over 12 pages needs a table of contents, table of authorities, and index of exhibits. Cite opposing arguments by docket and page, use the latest Bluebook, and keep captions free of counsel listings. No briefing schedules: L.R. 7.1(e) deadlines are enforced even if the hearing is far off, and a party that responds late may not argue. Most dispositive motions are heard; other motions at the court’s discretion. Motions may

docs.t: Judge Terrence G. Berg (E.D. Mich.) — Summary judgment (trap)
docs.x: Judge Terrence G. Berg, E.D. Mich.. Summary judgment (trap): One motion per party without leave. The motion must open with a numbered “Statement of Material Facts” with pinpoint record cites (counted against the page limit), and no separate narrative facts section. The response must open with a matching numbered “Counter-Statement of Material Facts” admitting or contesting each fact with record cites, plus any additional facts; uncontested facts are deemed admitted. Nonconforming briefs may be stricken without notice. File a tabbed, indexed Fact Appendix with the full text of cited sources. Avoid boilerplate standards and string cites; attach unpublished or specialty-reporter cases, though unpublished cases on Westlaw or Lexis need not be included in the appendix.

docs.t: Judge Terrence G. Berg (E.D. Mich.) — Chambers submissions and courtesy copies
docs.x: Judge Terrence G. Berg, E.D. Mich.. Chambers submissions and courtesy copies: No courtesy copies unless chambers requests them. Proposed orders, stipulations, witness lists, exhibit lists, jury instructions, voir dire questions, and verdict forms go to chambers through the CM/ECF Proposed Orders function in Word, not on the docket. Proposed orders on motions are encouraged before or at the hearing.

docs.t: Judge Terrence G. Berg (E.D. Mich.) — TROs, sealing, and remand
docs.x: Judge Terrence G. Berg, E.D. Mich.. TROs, sealing, and remand: All TRO requests, even ex parte ones, require some notice and a chance for both sides to be heard unless good cause is shown; the court usually holds a conference first and may shorten L.R. 7.1 deadlines. Call the case manager on filing. Sealing requires a motion under L.R. 5.3 with redacted and unredacted versions; protective orders do not authorize sealing, and only the confidential portions may be sealed. Criminal cooperation materials use a combined motion and proposed order submitted in Word through ECF Utilities. The court does not remand sua sponte; it issues an order to show cause. Motions to remand are typically argued, and procedural-defect remand motions must be filed within 30 days of removal.

docs.t: Judge Terrence G. Berg (E.D. Mich.) — Scheduling, discovery deadlines, and ADR
docs.x: Judge Terrence G. Berg, E.D. Mich.. Scheduling, discovery deadlines, and ADR: The scheduling conference notice issues 2–4 weeks after the answer (after all defendants answer, unless that causes significant delay, or after a dispositive motion is decided). Submit the Rule 26(f) plan and/or Case Summary at least one business day before; counsel must discuss ADR with clients first. Rule 26(a)(1) disclosures are generally due 14 days after the conference. Discovery must be served early enough to be answered before the cutoff. Stipulated extensions that are too long or lack good cause won’t be approved, and filing a motion doesn’t change deadlines. Deposition objections should be concise and few; privilege logs for ESI should include standard metadata fields. On joint request the court refers cases to case evaluation, private mediation, or a magistrate-judge settlement conference after discov

docs.t: Judge Terrence G. Berg (E.D. Mich.) — Civil pretrial and trial (trap)
docs.x: Judge Terrence G. Berg, E.D. Mich.. Civil pretrial and trial (trap): Trial is set after dispositive motions or a settlement conference, and adjournments are rarely granted. The Joint Final Pretrial Order must strictly follow L.R. 16.2; foundation and authenticity objections are waived unless a notice contesting foundation is filed at or before the final pretrial conference. The final pretrial conference (usually 1 week before trial) requires personal attendance of trial counsel, natural-person parties, a representative with full settlement authority, and any controlling insurer; phone availability doesn’t count. Witness lists are due 1 week before it, and joint voir dire, instructions, and verdict form must also be submitted; additional voir dire questions at least 3 days before it. Motions in limine are heard there. Make all exhibits available for inspection 1 week before the final pret

docs.t: Judge Terrence G. Berg (E.D. Mich.) — Criminal cases (trap)
docs.x: Judge Terrence G. Berg, E.D. Mich.. Criminal cases (trap): Counsel meet and confer within 10 days of arraignment; on request the government provides Rule 16(a)(1) material and Brady/Giglio material, listed and signed by all counsel, or moves for relief within the scheduling order’s 10-day period. Schedule changes go by stipulation with a proposed order and, if trial is affected, a Speedy Trial Act waiver. Absent a scheduling order, pretrial materials are due 1 week before the final pretrial conference (held 1–2 weeks before trial). Notices contesting foundation, chain of custody, or scientific analysis must be filed by that conference with an item-by-item good-faith basis. Proposed exhibits must be filed in the record within 5 business days of the verdict. Struck-jury system: usually 6 government and 10 defense peremptories, 12 jurors and 2 unidentified alternates. Sixth Circuit pattern

docs.t: Judge Terrence G. Berg (E.D. Mich.) — Patent cases
docs.x: Judge Terrence G. Berg, E.D. Mich.. Patent cases: The court uses a Model Rule 26(f) Report and Proposed Scheduling Order and automatically enters a Default Protective Order (CONFIDENTIAL and ATTORNEY’S EYES ONLY tiers; 10 days’ notice before disclosure to experts). Trial is typically 24–26 months after the scheduling conference per the Notice (the timeline chart says 22–24 months). The model order sequences infringement contentions, then invalidity and non-infringement contentions, then a technical-advisor settlement call, an unrecorded technology tutorial, and Markman briefs (25, 25, and 7 pages, 14-point) with a four-column claim chart. Live testimony at the Markman hearing requires a written motion and is typically limited to one hour per side. Liability and damages are normally bifurcated before the same jury.

docs.t: Judge Terrence G. Berg (E.D. Mich.) — Other
docs.x: Judge Terrence G. Berg, E.D. Mich.. Other: Out-of-state counsel eligible under L.R. 83.20 may take the oath by phone with the deputy clerk. Parties may consent to a magistrate judge for all proceedings, which may produce a firmer and sooner trial date.

docs.t: Judge Susan K. DeClercq (E.D. Mich.) — Discovery disputes (trap)
docs.x: Judge Susan K. DeClercq, E.D. Mich.. Discovery disputes (trap): The judge generally handles discovery disputes, and no discovery motion may be filed until the three-step protocol is complete: (1) meet and confer (an email exchange will not suffice; failing to make yourself available may draw sanctions); (2) email a joint letter to the case manager, generally no longer than 5 pages, identifying the dispute, the most important authority, and efforts to resolve it (a moving-party letter suffices if the dispute is solely a failure to respond); (3) an in-person conference with the court. Discovery cutoffs are strictly enforced and extended rarely, only for good cause. The court will not accept stipulations to extend discovery; ask for a status conference and explain the need.

docs.t: Judge Susan K. DeClercq (E.D. Mich.) — Motions
docs.x: Judge Susan K. DeClercq, E.D. Mich.. Motions: Before filing, seek concurrence under L.R. 7.1(a) through a good-faith effort to meet or have a real-time conversation (in person, video, or phone) with opposing counsel. Motions are decided on the briefs unless the court finds argument necessary or helpful; the case manager will send a hearing notice if so. No summary judgment motion before the end of discovery without leave.

docs.t: Judge Susan K. DeClercq (E.D. Mich.) — Judge’s copies (trap)
docs.x: Judge Susan K. DeClercq, E.D. Mich.. Judge’s copies (trap): Required only for dispositive motions and briefs, with all exhibits: indexed and tabbed, with copies of any case not on Westlaw or LEXIS, and with relevant parts of exhibits (such as deposition transcripts) and cases highlighted. Mail by first class the same day as e-filing, unless the filing relates to a proceeding within the next 5 days or needs immediate attention; then hand-deliver to chambers by the morning of the business day after e-filing.

docs.t: Judge Susan K. DeClercq (E.D. Mich.) — Proposed orders, record citations, and contact
docs.x: Judge Susan K. DeClercq, E.D. Mich.. Proposed orders, record citations, and contact: Do not e-file proposed or stipulated orders; submit them in Word through CM/ECF document utilities (ECF Rule R11). Stipulations with a non-e-filing pro se party must be e-filed with an actual signature, with only the proposed order sent through utilities. Allow 1 to 2 days for entry of a stipulated order. Cite the record strictly in ECF Rule R6 PageID form (e.g., PageID.234-235); for another E.D. Mich. case, precede it with the 13-character case number. No ex parte communications; staff answer procedural and scheduling questions only, after you check the guidelines, rules, and docket.

docs.t: Judge Susan K. DeClercq (E.D. Mich.) — TROs, emergencies, and status conferences
docs.x: Judge Susan K. DeClercq, E.D. Mich.. TROs, emergencies, and status conferences: The court strictly follows Rule 65 and L.R. 65.1 and rarely grants a TRO without notice. Call the case manager (313.234.5135) immediately on filing a TRO or preliminary injunction motion; a status conference usually follows to set briefing and a hearing. The court holds frequent status conferences (video or in person); contact the case manager to schedule one before an issue becomes an emergency.

docs.t: Judge Susan K. DeClercq (E.D. Mich.) — Civil scheduling and ADR
docs.x: Judge Susan K. DeClercq, E.D. Mich.. Civil scheduling and ADR: The court issues its Civil Case Practice Guidelines at assignment and, after an answer, a Notice Directing Parties to Appear for Scheduling Conference and Establishing Discovery Plan Deadline (Phase I). With multiple defendants, the conference usually waits for all answers unless that causes significant delay, but it proceeds even if one defendant has moved to dismiss. Early discovery by agreement is encouraged. ADR is typically ordered at the end of fact discovery; if the case doesn’t settle, the court then sets dispositive-motion through trial dates.

docs.t: Judge Susan K. DeClercq (E.D. Mich.) — Civil pretrial and trial (trap)
docs.x: Judge Susan K. DeClercq, E.D. Mich.. Civil pretrial and trial (trap): The proposed Joint Pretrial Order (L.R. 16.2 plus the Civil Case Practice Guidelines) is due before the Final Pretrial Hearing, typically 1–2 weeks before trial. Exhibit lists are due before that hearing after a meet-and-confer on admissibility; once a party inspects an opponent’s exhibit, foundation is presumed unless an objection is filed, and objections must be brought to the hearing. Jury instructions: jointly email the case manager one set of Stipulated Proposed Jury Instructions and, for disputes, Proposed Alternative Jury Instructions with objections and commentary, in Word, each on a separate page with authority and a table of contents. Skip standard introductory and concluding instructions. Each party uses a distinct consecutive exhibit numbering (preferably yellow “Plaintiff’s Exhibit 1” and blue “Defendant’s

docs.t: Judge Susan K. DeClercq (E.D. Mich.) — Criminal cases
docs.x: Judge Susan K. DeClercq, E.D. Mich.. Criminal cases: No initial status conference; the court issues a Scheduling Order. Changes need a motion or stipulation, plus a Speedy Trial Act waiver if the trial date is affected; one extension is routine, and a status conference often precedes more. Government and defense counsel must meet and confer within 10 days of arraignment on Rule 16 disclosure timing and procedures. All pretrial motions, responses, and replies must be filed before the Final Pretrial Hearing (L.R. 7.1(e), LCrR 12.1); proposed voir dire questions are due at least one week before that hearing, where the court will ask for an outline of plea offers and confirm any rejection. Signed Rule 11 plea agreements are due to chambers by the plea cutoff; the defendant must state the factual basis orally, by a method defense counsel confers on with the government and reports in advance.

docs.t: Judge David J. Novak (E.D. Va.) — Motion hearings (trap)
docs.x: Judge David J. Novak, E.D. Va.. Motion hearings (trap): In all civil cases assigned to Judge Novak, the court will not enforce Local Rule 7(E) to the extent it requires a movant to schedule a hearing within 30 days after filing a motion. Consistent with Local Rule 7(J), all motions are decided on the papers unless the court orders oral argument on its own or on a separate motion by the parties.

docs.t: Judge David J. Novak (E.D. Va.) — Requesting oral argument
docs.x: Judge David J. Novak, E.D. Va.. Requesting oral argument: A request for oral argument must be a separate motion with an incorporated brief explaining why oral argument will materially aid the decisional process. The court then decides whether to schedule a hearing on the underlying motion.

docs.t: Judge Brian Anthony Jackson (M.D. La.) — Contacting chambers (trap)
docs.x: Judge Brian Anthony Jackson, M.D. La.. Contacting chambers (trap): Do not contact the law clerks directly, and do not call chambers to ask about the status of a pending motion; updates will appear on the docket. Direct questions to the Clerk’s Office first; if still unanswered, contact the courtroom deputy, Javier Gutierrez (225-389-3694).

docs.t: Judge Brian Anthony Jackson (M.D. La.) — Extensions and continuances (trap)
docs.x: Judge Brian Anthony Jackson, M.D. La.. Extensions and continuances (trap): Do not contact chambers to ask for an extension or a continuance of a hearing, conference, or trial; file a motion. Once a motion is filed, call chambers to alert the courtroom deputy only if exigent circumstances require it. Motions for extensions of time filed within 48 hours of the deadline are strongly disfavored.

docs.t: Judge Brian Anthony Jackson (M.D. La.) — Proposed orders and judgments
docs.x: Judge Brian Anthony Jackson, M.D. La.. Proposed orders and judgments: Proposed orders must be filed as the last page of, or an attachment to, the motion and also emailed in an editable format, preferably Word, to baj_orders@lamd.uscourts.gov, with the case number in the subject line (for example, “06-451”). Proposed judgments ordered by the court are emailed in Word, not filed in CM/ECF, with the subject line “Proposed Judgment - [case number] BAJ.”

docs.t: Judge Brian Anthony Jackson (M.D. La.) — Pretrial conference and pretrial order (trap)
docs.x: Judge Brian Anthony Jackson, M.D. La.. Pretrial conference and pretrial order (trap): All trial counsel must participate in the pretrial conference; absent compelling circumstances, new counsel may not enroll after it is held. Before the final pretrial conference, trial counsel must meet and confer on jurisdiction, parties, joinder, settlement, Rule 26(a)(3) disclosures, narrowing issues, pending motions, and the proposed pretrial order. Plaintiff’s counsel must initiate the meeting; if another counsel won’t cooperate, promptly inform the court in writing. The joint pretrial order is due by the scheduling-order deadline, with no extensions absent good cause. It cannot be amended except by consent with leave of court or by court order to prevent manifest injustice, and must recite the prescribed joint pretrial statement above the signature lines.

docs.t: Judge Brian Anthony Jackson (M.D. La.) — Pretrial order contents
docs.x: Judge Brian Anthony Jackson, M.D. La.. Pretrial order contents: Include the nature of the action and jurisdiction (in diversity or amount-in-controversy cases, a joint stipulation that the amount is met or a brief statement on whether it could be awarded), abandoned claims, itemized relief and special damages, discovery status, pending motions, a comprehensive joint stipulation of uncontested facts, and disputed fact and law issues. Also state trial length, jury or non-jury, recommended number of jurors, positions on bifurcation, consent to a magistrate judge, and the history and status of settlement talks. No further discovery beyond the court’s deadlines absent good cause.

docs.t: Judge Brian Anthony Jackson (M.D. La.) — Exhibits, witnesses, and experts (trap)
docs.x: Judge Brian Anthony Jackson, M.D. La.. Exhibits, witnesses, and experts (trap): List exhibits (including demonstratives, but not impeachment or rebuttal items) with a brief description, whether authenticity is stipulated (and specific reasons if not), and each objection. Overlapping exhibits go on a joint list; duplicative exhibits won’t be admitted. Pre-mark and Bates-stamp all exhibits and be ready to give the court a Bench Book on a date set at the pretrial conference. List witnesses with addresses and a brief statement of testimony, plus objections. Provide a comprehensive joint stipulation of each expert’s qualifications; objections must refer to the corresponding motion in limine or Daubert motion, and duplicative expert testimony isn’t permitted. No unlisted exhibit, witness, expert, or deposition may be used in a party’s case in chief absent good cause.

docs.t: Judge Brian Anthony Jackson (M.D. La.) — Depositions and motions in limine
docs.x: Judge Brian Anthony Jackson, M.D. La.. Depositions and motions in limine: List depositions or portions to be used, with objections, and be ready to give the court the relevant transcript portions. Eliminate irrelevant and redundant material, including colloquy, when read at trial. Advise opposing counsel of a video deposition early enough for objections to be ruled on and edited out before trial. Motions in limine and Daubert motions follow the scheduling-order deadlines, and the pretrial order must list each disputed evidentiary issue with authority.

docs.t: Judge Brian Anthony Jackson (M.D. La.) — Jury instructions, voir dire, and findings
docs.x: Judge Brian Anthony Jackson, M.D. La.. Jury instructions, voir dire, and findings: Parties must confer and jointly submit proposed voir dire, jury instructions, and a verdict form by the scheduling-order deadlines. Where Louisiana law governs, use the Louisiana Civil Jury Instructions (Vol. 18, Louisiana Civil Law Treatise Series) if applicable; otherwise use Fifth Circuit pattern instructions first, then other federal pattern instructions. Requests to supplement instructions during or at the close of evidence are not granted absent good cause. In non-jury trials only, proposed findings of fact and conclusions of law are due on a date set at the pretrial conference.

docs.t: Judge Brian Anthony Jackson (M.D. La.) — Courtroom and trial (trap)
docs.x: Judge Brian Anthony Jackson, M.D. La.. Courtroom and trial (trap): Whoever will operate courtroom technology must contact the courtroom deputy at least 21 days before the hearing for a tutorial and bring the device. Requests to visit the courtroom must be made at least two weeks before the hearing or trial. Incarcerated parties must wear civilian clothing at trial, and counsel must arrange it. Uniformed witnesses (such as police or medical personnel) may not testify in uniform. Under Local Rule 83(b)(16): surnames are used, counsel may not roam the well, and all remarks are addressed to the court.

docs.t: Judge Shelly Deckert Dick (M.D. La.) — Pretrial order (trap)
docs.x: Judge Shelly Deckert Dick, M.D. La.. Pretrial order (trap): Plaintiff’s counsel prepares the pretrial order with all other counsel’s help; it must be signed by all counsel and submitted 14 days before the final pretrial conference. A party who disagrees with any part attaches an Opposition to the Pretrial Order before submission. A sample completed order is attached to the notice. Include jurisdiction, pending motions, each party’s claims, established facts, amendments, additional matters (settlement, ADR, magistrate-judge trial), jury or non-jury, and each side’s time estimate. Except for good cause, only exhibits and witnesses listed in the pretrial order (or a permitted amendment) will be admitted or allowed to testify.

docs.t: Judge Shelly Deckert Dick (M.D. La.) — Exhibits and witnesses
docs.x: Judge Shelly Deckert Dick, M.D. La.. Exhibits and witnesses: List all exhibits except impeachment-only documents, stating for each whether there are objections to authenticity (with reasons) and any objections to admissibility. Mark witnesses “will call” or “may call.” Will-call witnesses must be produced or subpoenaed by the listing party and kept available so opposing counsel can call them; may-call witnesses need not be subpoenaed. Give the court a witness list on the morning of trial; do not file it.

docs.t: Judge Shelly Deckert Dick (M.D. La.) — Deposition testimony (trap)
docs.x: Judge Shelly Deckert Dick, M.D. La.. Deposition testimony (trap): Designate deposition portions to be read or played no later than 28 days before trial; motions in limine on deposition objections are due 21 days before trial. Video depositions must be edited to a maximum of 30 minutes, and read depositions excerpted to a maximum of 30 pages. File a written transcript of any video deposition used, and supply a reader for any transcript read at trial.

docs.t: Judge Shelly Deckert Dick (M.D. La.) — Jury instructions (trap)
docs.x: Judge Shelly Deckert Dick, M.D. La.. Jury instructions (trap): Joint jury instructions, including a joint verdict or interrogatory form, are due 21 days before trial. No separate filings: all submissions must be joint, with disagreements footnoted with case authority and pinpoint cites. Fifth Circuit pattern instructions may be cited by number and edition. The jury-trial notice separately sets requested voir dire, proposed jury charges, and motions in limine for filing 14 days before trial; follow the dates in your case’s notice.

docs.t: Judge Shelly Deckert Dick (M.D. La.) — JERS electronic evidence (trap)
docs.x: Judge Shelly Deckert Dick, M.D. La.. JERS electronic evidence (trap): Each party submits electronic evidence files (an Electronic Bench Book) through the court’s Electronic Evidence Online tool in CM/ECF to the courtroom deputy 7 days before trial or any evidentiary proceeding, in the format on the court’s courtroom technology tab. These are for the court only and are not given to opponents; conventional bench books are no longer needed. Evidence admitted but not previously submitted, and any substitutions, go to the deputy during a recess or before the next day’s session. Exhibits used at trial must match the submitted files in number and image. JERS is not used to present evidence: use a laptop connection or the document camera in Courtroom 3, and contact the courtroom deputy, Suzie Edwards, to schedule equipment training before trial.

docs.t: Judge Shelly Deckert Dick (M.D. La.) — Trial
docs.x: Judge Shelly Deckert Dick, M.D. La.. Trial: Opening statements are limited to 30 minutes per side and closing arguments to 1 hour per side. The pretrial conference is held in chambers. A party or party representative with full authority to compromise must attend trial. After trial, parties keep custody of physical exhibits and must preserve them, make them available to opposing counsel, and transmit them to the appellate court if required. Avoid eliciting personal identifying information in testimony or argument.

docs.t: Judge Shelly Deckert Dick (M.D. La.) — Settlement affidavit and costs (trap)
docs.x: Judge Shelly Deckert Dick, M.D. La.. Settlement affidavit and costs (trap): By the scheduling-order deadline, each side’s counsel files an affidavit stating the date and time of a settlement conference of counsel. Plaintiff’s counsel attests to making a good-faith offer and conveying the counteroffer; defense counsel attests to conveying the offer and making a good-faith counteroffer. State no dollar amounts. A party who refuses an offer and then does worse at judgment may be ordered to pay the other side’s later costs, including expert and witness fees but not attorney’s fees, unless good cause is shown. If a jury case settles within 3 business days before trial or later, jury venire costs will be taxed; immediate notice to the Clerk and the court may avoid this.

docs.t: Judge Shelly Deckert Dick (M.D. La.) — Settlement notice
docs.x: Judge Shelly Deckert Dick, M.D. La.. Settlement notice: A call to chambers giving informal notice of settlement is appreciated, but the Local Rules’ required joint notice of settlement must still be filed.

docs.t: Judge Shelly Deckert Dick (M.D. La.) — Proposed orders and judgments
docs.x: Judge Shelly Deckert Dick, M.D. La.. Proposed orders and judgments: Proposed orders must be filed as the last page of, or an attachment to, the motion and also emailed in an editable format, preferably Word, to sdd_orders@lamd.uscourts.gov, with the case number in the subject line (for example, “06-451”). Proposed judgments ordered by the court are emailed in Word, not filed in CM/ECF, with the subject line “Proposed Judgment - [case number] SDD.”

docs.t: Judge Stephen N. Limbaugh Jr. (E.D. Mo.) — Motions and memoranda (trap)
docs.x: Judge Stephen N. Limbaugh Jr., E.D. Mo.. Motions and memoranda (trap): Motions and memoranda must comply with Local Rule 4.01 and use Times New Roman 13 point (or a comparable font). If that pushes a memorandum over the page limit, file a short motion for leave to exceed it. Joint motions must be signed by counsel for all parties and any pro se parties. Convert documents to PDF by printing or publishing, not scanning, except for procedural motions (extensions, pro hac vice, process-server notices).

docs.t: Judge Stephen N. Limbaugh Jr. (E.D. Mo.) — Courtesy copies (trap)
docs.x: Judge Stephen N. Limbaugh Jr., E.D. Mo.. Courtesy copies (trap): In civil and criminal cases, submit a paper courtesy copy to chambers of any motion or memorandum that, with exhibits, exceeds 50 pages. Mail it to chambers or hand-deliver it to the Clerk’s Office in Cape Girardeau.

docs.t: Judge Stephen N. Limbaugh Jr. (E.D. Mo.) — Proposed orders and judgments
docs.x: Judge Stephen N. Limbaugh Jr., E.D. Mo.. Proposed orders and judgments: File proposed orders and judgments as a PDF attachment to the related motion or memorandum, and also email them in Word to Kimberly_Price@moed.uscourts.gov.

docs.t: Judge Stephen N. Limbaugh Jr. (E.D. Mo.) — Conferences and deadline changes
docs.x: Judge Stephen N. Limbaugh Jr., E.D. Mo.. Conferences and deadline changes: Informal matters and status conferences are not regularly held; call chambers to set one in chambers or by telephone. Most minor, agreed deadline changes can be handled by a motion to extend stating that opposing counsel consents; consent motions are ruled on as soon as possible.

docs.t: Judge Stephen N. Limbaugh Jr. (E.D. Mo.) — Rule 16 conference and CMO
docs.x: Judge Stephen N. Limbaugh Jr., E.D. Mo.. Rule 16 conference and CMO: A Rule 16 conference is set after all defendants answer. The attorney preparing and trying the case must appear unless the court permits another; parties may participate by telephone with prior notice. If the case is ready and no conference is set, notify the judicial assistant. The resulting Case Management Order has a Scheduling Order (all deadlines) and an Order Relating to Trial (pretrial requirements); counsel should consult it throughout the case.

docs.t: Judge Stephen N. Limbaugh Jr. (E.D. Mo.) — Docket location
docs.x: Judge Stephen N. Limbaugh Jr., E.D. Mo.. Docket location: Trials and non-expedited hearings on the St. Louis docket are generally set in St. Louis the third week of each month; Cape Girardeau docket matters are heard in Cape Girardeau at all other times. The judge sits in Courtroom 4B, Cape Girardeau.

docs.t: Judge Stephen N. Limbaugh Jr. (E.D. Mo.) — ADR (trap)
docs.x: Judge Stephen N. Limbaugh Jr., E.D. Mo.. ADR (trap): Civil cases (except habeas) are referred to ADR as set in the CMO. Lead counsel (plaintiff’s counsel or agreed counsel) must work with opposing counsel to select a neutral and notify the judicial assistant no later than 20 days from the start of the referral. ADR deadlines are binding and extendable only by court order. On settlement, notify the court immediately and file a Rule 41(a)(1)(A)(ii) joint stipulation of dismissal or proposed consent judgment within 30 days. Also notify the court if no settlement is reached.

docs.t: Judge Stephen N. Limbaugh Jr. (E.D. Mo.) — Sealing and protective orders (trap)
docs.x: Judge Stephen N. Limbaugh Jr., E.D. Mo.. Sealing and protective orders (trap): A proposed protective order contemplating sealed filings must state a date certain when the seal will be lifted or documents returned; one without it will be denied without prejudice. See also Local Rule 13.05.

docs.t: Judge Stephen N. Limbaugh Jr. (E.D. Mo.) — Trial
docs.x: Judge Stephen N. Limbaugh Jr., E.D. Mo.. Trial: Court ordinarily runs 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 or 5:30 p.m. Raise preliminary matters at the pretrial conference, not at the start of a trial day. The court asks initial voir dire questions, then counsel may question subject to time limits set at the pretrial conference; if the court conducts all voir dire, submit questions at least three days before trial. Jury instructions follow the CMO, and opening and closing time limits are set at the pretrial conference. Disclose the identity and order of witnesses at least 24 hours before the trial day they’ll be called, and have enough witnesses to fill the day. Request equipment (ELMO) training from the Case Management Team at least one week before trial.

docs.t: Judge Stephen N. Limbaugh Jr. (E.D. Mo.) — Courtroom conduct
docs.x: Judge Stephen N. Limbaugh Jr., E.D. Mo.. Courtroom conduct: No evidentiary objections argued before the jury; ask for a bench conference. Sidebars are disfavored. Recross is allowed only if redirect brings out something new. Stand when speaking and objecting and when the jury enters; ask permission to approach a witness or the bench. Address witnesses by last name and title, and direct statements to the court. No visible reactions to testimony or rulings at counsel table (violators may be ejected; signaling a witness is contempt). No food, drink other than water, or gum.

docs.t: Judge John Phil Gilbert (S.D. Ill.) — Proposed orders (trap)
docs.x: Judge John Phil Gilbert, S.D. Ill.. Proposed orders (trap): A movant must email a proposed order for every motion filed to JPGpd@ilsd.uscourts.gov.

docs.t: Judge John Phil Gilbert (S.D. Ill.) — Motions
docs.x: Judge John Phil Gilbert, S.D. Ill.. Motions: Civil motions must conform to Local Rule 7.1. Oral argument may be requested but is discretionary. Criminal pretrial motions ordinarily must be filed within 21 days after arraignment, with a supporting memorandum of law. The court adheres strictly to all statutory and local-rule time limits.

docs.t: Judge John Phil Gilbert (S.D. Ill.) — Final pretrial order (trap)
docs.x: Judge John Phil Gilbert, S.D. Ill.. Final pretrial order (trap): Plaintiff’s attorney has primary responsibility for preparing it, with full cooperation from defense counsel. Submit it to the trial judge 3 days before the final pretrial conference unless otherwise directed. Noncompliance can draw sanctions under Rules 16 and 37 and 28 U.S.C. § 1927. The form covers nature of the case, jurisdiction, uncontroverted facts, agreed issues of law, witnesses (expert and non-expert), itemized damages, bifurcation, and trial length; rebuttal witnesses need no prior notice. Attach a separate Pretrial Exhibit Stipulation listing each party’s numbered exhibits (other than impeachment) with objections and grounds; plaintiff bears the burden of timely submitting a complete list. Stipulate to authenticity and state specific reasons where not stipulated. Each party supplies a pre-marked copy of each exh

docs.t: Judge John Phil Gilbert (S.D. Ill.) — Voir dire and jury selection
docs.x: Judge John Phil Gilbert, S.D. Ill.. Voir dire and jury selection: The court conducts voir dire. On request, in civil and single-defendant criminal cases, counsel may question the panel, preferably as a whole, for 15 minutes per side unless leave is given. Challenges for cause are taken at sidebar first. Civil: 6 jurors, 3 peremptories per side, 14 panel members called, juries picked in panels of three (four for the first panel if parties agree to a 7-person jury), with plaintiff exercising first. Criminal: 12 jurors, 6 peremptories for the government and 10 for the defense, 28 panel members called, picked in panels of four with the government first; typically two alternates, with 1 extra peremptory per side for alternates only.

docs.t: Judge John Phil Gilbert (S.D. Ill.) — Witnesses (trap)
docs.x: Judge John Phil Gilbert, S.D. Ill.. Witnesses (trap): Unlisted witnesses are barred unless leave is granted for good cause. Don’t run out of witnesses: have them assembled and ready, and have a witness on the stand at a recess back on the stand when court resumes. Doctors and other professionals may be taken out of sequence; discuss it with opposing counsel in advance and confer with the court if there is an objection. Instruct witnesses to dress suitably.

docs.t: Judge John Phil Gilbert (S.D. Ill.) — Examination, objections, and decorum
docs.x: Judge John Phil Gilbert, S.D. Ill.. Examination, objections, and decorum: Examine from the lectern, counsel table, or end of the jury box; seated examination needs permission. No permission is needed to approach a witness, but the court prefers it only when absolutely necessary. Rise when addressing the court and when objecting. State only the objection and its grounds, with no speeches; argument only when the court permits or requests it. Opening statements must not argue the case or instruct on the law. No colloquy between attorneys; address remarks, including re-reading requests, to the court. Confer with opposing counsel before offering a stipulation in a jury case, and avoid first names.

docs.t: Judge John Phil Gilbert (S.D. Ill.) — Exhibits and depositions
docs.x: Judge John Phil Gilbert, S.D. Ill.. Exhibits and depositions: Number exhibits consecutively, have copies for the court and opposing counsel, and show them to opposing counsel before use. Return exhibits to the Clerk at each noon and end-of-day break. Offer exhibits when they become admissible, and mark exhibits only with the court’s permission. Mark all depositions used at trial as exhibits; when impeaching, state page and line before reading. For answers to interrogatories or requests for admission drawn from several documents, prepare a compiled document with copies for the court and opposing counsel.

docs.t: Judge John Phil Gilbert (S.D. Ill.) — Difficult issues
docs.x: Judge John Phil Gilbert, S.D. Ill.. Difficult issues: Give the court advance notice of any difficult question of law or evidence, ideally by a brief or memorandum submitted before trial.

docs.t: Judge Curtis Lynn Collier (E.D. Tenn.) — Motions and oral argument (trap)
docs.x: Judge Curtis Lynn Collier, E.D. Tenn.. Motions and oral argument (trap): The judge typically does not hold oral argument on motions and will set it if useful. To ask for argument, file a separate motion explaining why it would be of particular benefit. Requests for pages beyond Local Rule 7.1(b) are granted only in the most exceptional cases; move at least two business days before the long document is due, stating all parties’ positions if possible. Put citations to authority in the text, not in footnotes or endnotes. Dispositive motions (Rule 12 and Rule 56) must be filed as soon as possible and by the scheduling-order deadline; untimely motions may be summarily denied.

docs.t: Judge Curtis Lynn Collier (E.D. Tenn.) — Chambers contact and courtesy copies
docs.x: Judge Curtis Lynn Collier, E.D. Tenn.. Chambers contact and courtesy copies: Written correspondence to the court is discouraged; if sent, copy all counsel. Requests for action go by motion or other filing. Law clerks handle only purely administrative matters, and calls to chambers should include a representative of each side whenever possible. No courtesy copies unless specifically requested, except that jury instruction requests (and proposed findings and conclusions in bench trials) must be emailed in Word or a compatible format to collier_chambers@tned.uscourts.gov.

docs.t: Judge Curtis Lynn Collier (E.D. Tenn.) — Conferences and scheduling (trap)
docs.x: Judge Curtis Lynn Collier, E.D. Tenn.. Conferences and scheduling (trap): Counsel who will be actively involved and who have authority to bind their party must attend the scheduling conference and final pretrial conference in person. The judge may initiate telephone conferences in other situations. The judge uses a standard scheduling order (no need to complete the form before the conference) and generally defers to reasonable input on the discovery period and trial month. A Rule 26(f) discovery plan is due within 14 days after the Rule 26(f) meeting if not already filed. If no joinder or amendment deadline is proposed at the conference, it is 45 days from entry of the scheduling order. Changing the trial date does not move the other scheduled dates; seek any other change by motion. Extensions that don’t affect the trial date or the court’s ability to decide a dispositive motion are more

docs.t: Judge Curtis Lynn Collier (E.D. Tenn.) — Discovery and experts
docs.x: Judge Curtis Lynn Collier, E.D. Tenn.. Discovery and experts: Discovery disputes that counsel can’t resolve under the local rule go to the assigned magistrate judge. Any party seeking a Daubert hearing must move by the scheduling-order deadline; the court sets a hearing date for such motions in the order. Do not deliver expert reports to the court. Final witness lists may be supplemented within 7 days after service, and afterward only with leave for good cause. All deposition testimony to be offered at trial must be disclosed by the pretrial disclosure date.

docs.t: Judge Curtis Lynn Collier (E.D. Tenn.) — Emergency relief
docs.x: Judge Curtis Lynn Collier, E.D. Tenn.. Emergency relief: TRO and preliminary injunction requests must comply with Rule 65. The judge will have the movant notify the opposing party when an emergency hearing is set, often the same day the petition is filed, so be ready to appear. Expedited discovery and briefing are allowed before a preliminary injunction hearing; proposed findings and conclusions are welcome.

docs.t: Judge Curtis Lynn Collier (E.D. Tenn.) — Final pretrial conference and order (trap)
docs.x: Judge Curtis Lynn Collier, E.D. Tenn.. Final pretrial conference and order (trap): The final pretrial conference is held in chambers on a Thursday at 4:00 p.m. Submit the proposed final pretrial order (on the judge’s posted form) no later than one business day before the conference. The order covers jurisdiction, claims, stipulated facts, each side’s theory, contested legal issues, exhibits that can’t be stipulated as admissible, and witnesses with addresses and phone numbers. Bring three copies of the joint exhibit list; in a nonjury case, furnish a copy of each exhibit at the conference. The final pretrial order supplants the pleadings, and the form warns that omitting a jury demand from it may be argued to waive the jury, so state the demand expressly.

docs.t: Judge Curtis Lynn Collier (E.D. Tenn.) — Electronic exhibits (trap)
docs.x: Judge Curtis Lynn Collier, E.D. Tenn.. Electronic exhibits (trap): Trials use all exhibits in electronic format through the courtroom evidence presentation system; paper documents should not be used. Jurors view electronic exhibits on a system in the jury room rather than receiving physical copies; firearms and controlled substances do not go to the jury room. At least 7 days before the final pretrial conference, disclose to each other and the court the technology you will use (equipment you bring and court equipment you will use), and confirm compatibility by the conference. Exhibits are strongly encouraged to go to the courtroom deputy at the final pretrial conference or at least 7 days before trial.

docs.t: Judge Curtis Lynn Collier (E.D. Tenn.) — Jury instructions and findings
docs.x: Judge Curtis Lynn Collier, E.D. Tenn.. Jury instructions and findings: Requests for jury instructions are due by the scheduling-order date under Local Rule 51.1, with citations under Local Rule 7.4, filed and emailed in Word. Parties must confer, try to resolve disagreements, and submit joint instructions to the extent possible, following the form of the Sixth Circuit Criminal Pattern Jury Instructions (as the civil scheduling order states). Bench trials: proposed findings must include a jurisdictional statement, identify the parties, and set out facts in the chronological order the party intends to prove them; conclusions of law must be concise, cited, and not argumentative.

docs.t: Judge Curtis Lynn Collier (E.D. Tenn.) — Trial
docs.x: Judge Curtis Lynn Collier, E.D. Tenn.. Trial: A date certain for trial, typically a Monday, is set at the scheduling conference and rarely moved. Be present at 9:00 a.m. on day one; if not reached, the case is held in line through the trial week. Examine from the lectern, standing. More than one lawyer may try the case, but only one per witness may examine and object. Examination beyond redirect is discouraged, though recross is occasionally allowed. Sidebars are discouraged; raise issues at breaks and alert the deputy or law clerk in advance. The judge conducts all voir dire but welcomes proposed questions. No time limit on openings; counsel’s input is considered on closings. Exhibits are pre-marked per the parties’ list, with three copies of the list to the courtroom deputy before trial. Trial briefs are encouraged but not required. Stay in the courthouse during deliberations.

docs.t: Judge Curtis Lynn Collier (E.D. Tenn.) — Criminal cases (trap)
docs.x: Judge Curtis Lynn Collier, E.D. Tenn.. Criminal cases (trap): Trial practices match civil. Plea and motion deadlines hold unless modified on motion, and the court generally will not accept a plea agreement executed after the plea deadline. At sentencing, no character-witness testimony; witnesses testify only on factual disputes that could affect the Guideline range. Letters of support submitted before the hearing and counsel’s proffers of what a character witness would say are accepted.

docs.t: Judge Curtis Lynn Collier (E.D. Tenn.) — Settlement and media
docs.x: Judge Curtis Lynn Collier, E.D. Tenn.. Settlement and media: Parties are urged to settle in all cases, using mediation or other ADR if needed; magistrate judges may be involved case by case. Local Rule 83.2 governs media contact, and the judge discourages any communication about pending cases.

docs.t: Judge Mary Elizabeth Phillips (W.D. Mo.) — Oral argument for new lawyers (trap)
docs.x: Judge Mary Elizabeth Phillips, W.D. Mo.. Oral argument for new lawyers (trap): Requests for oral argument are considered under Local Rule 7.0(e). In addition, Judge Phillips automatically grants oral argument on a contested motion if the requesting party certifies the argument will be presented by a lawyer who graduated from law school within six years before the motion was filed. The request must expressly invoke this policy and appear on the first page of the motion or suggestions in support (movant), or on the first page of the responding party’s first filing addressing the motion (opposition, request for more time, etc.).

docs.t: Judge Mary Elizabeth Phillips (W.D. Mo.) — Proposed scheduling order
docs.x: Judge Mary Elizabeth Phillips, W.D. Mo.. Proposed scheduling order: Hold the Rule 26(f) meeting no later than 14 days before the proposed scheduling order is due; discovery starts immediately after it. File one joint proposed order signed by both sides (no signature line for the judge) under Other Filings – Other documents – Proposed Scheduling Order. Include a proposed trial date, trial length, and jury or bench; dates for adding parties and amending pleadings; discovery completion; expert designations; and the dispositive-motion deadline. Expected spacing: discovery closes 6 months before trial; dispositive motions 5 months before trial; experts designated 4 months before the discovery deadline; trial typically 150 days after the dispositive-motion deadline. The court sets a settlement-status teleconference 4–5 weeks before trial and the pretrial conference about 2 weeks before trial.

docs.t: Judge Mary Elizabeth Phillips (W.D. Mo.) — Discovery disputes (trap)
docs.x: Judge Mary Elizabeth Phillips, W.D. Mo.. Discovery disputes (trap): No discovery motion is entertained without full compliance with Local Rule 37.1. Request a teleconference by email to the judicial assistant (annette_cordell@mow.uscourts.gov); each party then submits a memorandum of the dispute, no more than one page, at least 48 hours before the teleconference. Discovery must be completed, not merely served, by the deadline.

docs.t: Judge Mary Elizabeth Phillips (W.D. Mo.) — Experts
docs.x: Judge Mary Elizabeth Phillips, W.D. Mo.. Experts: Each designated expert, retained or non-retained, must provide a Rule 26(a)(2)(B) report with the designation, and may testify only to matters in the report absent leave for good cause. For treating physicians and similar non-retained professionals, producing all of the provider’s files, records, and notes satisfies the report requirement, but testimony beyond the treatment provided requires designation as an expert and full compliance.

docs.t: Judge Mary Elizabeth Phillips (W.D. Mo.) — Dispositive motions
docs.x: Judge Mary Elizabeth Phillips, W.D. Mo.. Dispositive motions: Dispositive motions (other than Rule 12(h)(2) or (3)) must include a separate section of individually numbered facts, and suggestions in opposition must begin with a concise list of the material facts claimed to be genuinely disputed. Summary judgment motions must comply with Local Rules 7.0 and 56.1.

docs.t: Judge Mary Elizabeth Phillips (W.D. Mo.) — Pretrial filings (trap)
docs.x: Judge Mary Elizabeth Phillips, W.D. Mo.. Pretrial filings (trap): Before the pretrial conference: motions in limine 10 days before (responses 3 days before); witness and exhibit lists 5 days before (unlisted witnesses and exhibits are excluded absent leave); trial briefs (optional) and voir dire questions 5 days before; stipulation of uncontroverted facts (or a joint statement that none can be agreed, including on jurisdiction) and stipulation on admissibility 3 days before. The procedures document adds that a preserved request to stipulate counts as a Rule 36 request for admission, so refusing can draw Rule 37(c) sanctions, and that each exhibit must be numbered and listed on the clerk’s exhibit-index form for the courtroom deputy. Deposition designations by page and line 15 days before the pretrial conference; objections and counter-designations 10 days before; objections to counter-de

docs.t: Judge Mary Elizabeth Phillips (W.D. Mo.) — Jury instructions
docs.x: Judge Mary Elizabeth Phillips, W.D. Mo.. Jury instructions: File one joint annotated set 3 days before the pretrial conference, drawn from the Eighth Circuit model civil instructions and/or MAI, each numbered “Instruction No. ___” without showing which party proposed it (the procedures document also asks for a clean set without sources). Email a Word version to the judicial assistant. Separate instructions only where the parties cannot agree: each side submits its version with a written objection to the other’s; the procedures document requires stated reasons, authority, and an alternative instruction, due one week before trial.

docs.t: Judge Mary Elizabeth Phillips (W.D. Mo.) — Trial and settlement (trap)
docs.x: Judge Mary Elizabeth Phillips, W.D. Mo.. Trial and settlement (trap): Jury trials begin at 8:30 a.m. in Kansas City. Settlement deadline is 12:00 noon on the business day before trial; later settlements may draw an order to show cause on costs. Test courtroom equipment before trial; technology, interpreter, and video-conference requests go to the courtroom deputy at least 5 days before the event (court-wide policy).

docs.t: Judge Bernard M. Jones (W.D. Okla.) — Communicating with the court (trap)
docs.x: Judge Bernard M. Jones, W.D. Okla.. Communicating with the court (trap): Every request to the court or notification about a case must be in writing and filed properly; a phone call does not suffice. Procedural questions go to Courtroom Deputy D. Wayne Lee (405-609-5042, D_Wayne_Lee@okwd.uscourts.gov). Send proposed orders to jones-orders@okwd.uscourts.gov.

docs.t: Judge Bernard M. Jones (W.D. Okla.) — Pending motions (trap)
docs.x: Judge Bernard M. Jones, W.D. Okla.. Pending motions (trap): The moving party must email the courtroom deputy if any motion has been pending more than 90 days after it is fully briefed.

docs.t: Judge Bernard M. Jones (W.D. Okla.) — Proposed orders
docs.x: Judge Bernard M. Jones, W.D. Okla.. Proposed orders: Proposed orders must be in Times New Roman, 12 point, fully justified.

docs.t: Judge Bernard M. Jones (W.D. Okla.) — Discovery disputes
docs.x: Judge Bernard M. Jones, W.D. Okla.. Discovery disputes: The judge expects parties to resolve discovery disputes without the court and will award attorney fees or impose other sanctions if a dispute unnecessarily wastes judicial resources. The meet-and-confer requirement is strictly enforced: counsel must personally confer in good faith. If a hearing is set, the judge may require counsel to meet and confer again before it.

docs.t: Judge Bernard M. Jones (W.D. Okla.) — Extensions of dispositive and Daubert deadlines (trap)
docs.x: Judge Bernard M. Jones, W.D. Okla.. Extensions of dispositive and Daubert deadlines (trap): The interval between the dispositive and Daubert motion deadline and the trial docket is relatively inflexible. Do not assume an extension of that deadline, or of the response time, will be granted; a strong showing is required, and failing to do discovery earlier usually won’t justify one. Any extension of those motion deadlines will likely also postpone the trial docket, perhaps significantly, whether or not requested.

docs.t: Judge Bernard M. Jones (W.D. Okla.) — Mediation and settlement conferences (trap)
docs.x: Judge Bernard M. Jones, W.D. Okla.. Mediation and settlement conferences (trap): Early mediation is strongly encouraged. Lead trial counsel must attend any judicial settlement conference, with a party or representative with full authority if counsel lacks it. Do not plan to be lead counsel at trial if you did not attend the settlement conference.

docs.t: Judge Bernard M. Jones (W.D. Okla.) — Trial exhibits and logistics
docs.x: Judge Bernard M. Jones, W.D. Okla.. Trial exhibits and logistics: Immediately before trial, each party gives the courtroom deputy three sets of its witness list, exhibit list, and exhibit notebooks. Exhibits are numbered, include the case number, and go in tabbed three-ring binders; court time may not be used for marking. The third set, with original stickers, is the record copy on the witness stand. Exhibits are ordinarily shown by overhead projector or similar means, not passed to the jury, and may not be published before admission. Daily copy or other extraordinary reporter services require notice to the Chief Deputy Court Clerk at least two weeks before the case is set to be called for trial. No food or beverages in the courtroom.

docs.t: Judge Bernard M. Jones (W.D. Okla.) — Courtroom conduct at trial
docs.x: Judge Bernard M. Jones, W.D. Okla.. Courtroom conduct at trial: Stand to address the court (including objections) and to question witnesses; stay at the lectern unless given permission to approach. Openings are a concise factual summary with no argument or law, limited to 10 minutes per party unless the case is unusually complex. Objections before the jury must be short, without argument; make motions at the first recess. Only the attorney handling a witness may object or respond regarding that witness. Address witnesses by surname (except children), skip greetings on cross, don’t face the jurors while questioning, and don’t react visibly to testimony or leave the courtroom without leave. Give the court as much notice as possible of difficult legal or evidentiary questions. docs.t: Judge Charles Barnes Goodwin (W.D. Okla.) — Trial day schedule (trap)
docs.x: Judge Charles Barnes Goodwin, W.D. Okla.. Trial day schedule (trap): All trial counsel must be present at 9:00 a.m. to discuss legal or evidentiary issues expected that day. Evidence comes in three uninterrupted sessions: 9:30–11:30 a.m., 12:30–2:30 p.m., and 3:00–5:00 p.m. Sessions may run longer but will not be shortened: be ready to ask the first question at the start and to keep calling witnesses until the session ends.

docs.t: Judge Charles Barnes Goodwin (W.D. Okla.) — Electronic exhibits (trap)
docs.x: Judge Charles Barnes Goodwin, W.D. Okla.. Electronic exhibits (trap): Unless otherwise ordered, present exhibits to witnesses and the jury electronically through the JERS system, with paper only as backup. A technology conference with the courtroom deputy is set at docket call (or earlier on request). Immediately before trial, give the court and opposing counsel your exhibits in a JERS-compatible electronic format with the labels that system needs.

docs.t: Judge Charles Barnes Goodwin (W.D. Okla.) — Paper submissions at trial
docs.x: Judge Charles Barnes Goodwin, W.D. Okla.. Paper submissions at trial: Immediately before trial, give the courtroom deputy a witness list, an exhibit list, and one exhibit notebook: a three-ring binder with a cover sheet showing the case number and sponsoring party, exhibits numbered as on the list and tabbed, including originals marked with original-document stickers. The deputy keeps it and places exhibits before witnesses.

docs.t: Judge James Donald Peterson (W.D. Wis.) — Attorney fees
docs.x: Judge James Donald Peterson, W.D. Wis.. Attorney fees: Fee requests must state the legal basis and include contemporaneous task-by-task logs showing who did the work, hourly rates, a billing-judgment affidavit, and market-rate evidence (an affidavit of the attorney’s “usual” rate is typically insufficient). Inadequate support may lead to a reduced award or none. Opponents must state with particularity what is unreasonable, and parties should stipulate to reasonable hours or rates. Without evidence that the client assigned a statutory fee right to the attorney, fees may be paid directly to the client.

docs.t: Judge James Donald Peterson (W.D. Wis.) — Settlements and dismissals (trap)
docs.x: Judge James Donald Peterson, W.D. Wis.. Settlements and dismissals (trap): An informal settlement does not take a case off the trial calendar; file a stipulation or joint motion. A notice of dismissal with prejudice ends the court’s jurisdiction, so the court cannot retain jurisdiction to enforce a settlement (Dupuy v. McEwen). If a case resolves the weekend before trial, contact the Clerk of Court at (608) 354-8004.

docs.t: Judge James Donald Peterson (W.D. Wis.) — Trial logistics
docs.x: Judge James Donald Peterson, W.D. Wis.. Trial logistics: The standard instructions tell jurors the trial day runs 9:00 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. and that they may submit written questions for witnesses and take notes. Counsel rooms are not guaranteed; request one at (608) 264-5156. Rooms are assigned randomly the Wednesday before trial, and if not every party can get one, none is assigned. Contacting jurors requires the court’s permission (LR 47.2), requested at the final pretrial conference or soon after trial; only counsel may make contact, using details the clerk supplies.

docs.t: Judge James Donald Peterson (W.D. Wis.) — Witnesses for pro se litigants
docs.x: Judge James Donald Peterson, W.D. Wis.. Witnesses for pro se litigants: Most deadlines are four weeks before trial: motions for writs to bring incarcerated witnesses and requests for subpoena forms for unwilling witnesses, with supporting affidavits. Subpoenas should reach the Marshal at least two weeks before trial, with witness fees and mileage tendered for unincarcerated witnesses.

docs.t: Judge William Martin Conley (W.D. Wis.) — Summary judgment: proposed findings of fact (trap)
docs.x: Judge William Martin Conley, W.D. Wis.. Summary judgment: proposed findings of fact (trap): The motion must come with a separate statement of proposed findings of fact (or a stipulation of facts), evidentiary materials, and a brief. Each fact goes in its own numbered paragraph, limited as nearly as possible to a single proposition, followed by a pinpoint citation to supporting evidence (for depositions, witness name, date, and page; for affidavits, affiant, date, page, and paragraph). The proposed findings must include ALL facts needed for judgment, including jurisdiction, the parties’ identities, and the context of the dispute. The court will not consider facts that appear only in a brief, and it will not search the record for evidence. Documents must be authenticated by affidavit or stipulation; an unauthenticated copy is not accepted as evidence.

docs.t: Judge William Martin Conley (W.D. Wis.) — Summary judgment: responses and replies (trap)
docs.x: Judge William Martin Conley, W.D. Wis.. Summary judgment: responses and replies (trap): The opponent must answer each proposed fact in a separate paragraph using the same number; any fact not put in dispute is deemed undisputed. A dispute must state the party’s version and cite admissible evidence, and new facts not directly responsive are disregarded. The court prefers (but does not require) repeating each proposed fact verbatim before the response. Additional facts go in the opponent’s own proposed findings, which supplement but never replace the separate response to the movant’s facts. The movant’s reply must repeat verbatim the whole sequence for each fact (proposal, response, reply) so it is a self-contained history; the movant answers any additional proposed facts at the same time. docs.t: Judge William Martin Conley (W.D. Wis.) — Trial conduct
docs.x: Judge William Martin Conley, W.D. Wis.. Trial conduct: Have all witnesses and evidence ready: trial may move faster than expected and may run into the evening to finish in the time promised the jury. Under the judge’s February 1, 2018 order, failure can preclude a party from presenting further evidence. The standard remarks tell jurors the trial day generally runs 8:30 a.m. to 5:30 p.m., and the instructions let jurors submit written questions for witnesses after counsel finish.
